answer: The paper explores domains defined as news publications (data sources), extending the conventional category-based definition of domain to article sources, with the top five publications used as source domains for training and the bottom ones treated as OUT-OF-DOMAIN [3][4][6][10]. Specifically, it focuses on extractive summarization and demonstrates that news publications can cause data distribution differences, meaning they can themselves be defined as domains [10]. The paper assumes K related domains, each represented as a dataset Dk, to study multi-domain summarization [8].

The paper assumes K related domains, each represented as a dataset Dk, to study multi-domain summarization [8].
